record.paper_title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems
record.context_brief: Concrete interpretability and NN-visualization use cases
record.original_question: What concrete use cases can make interpretability and transparency methods for safety-critical machine-learning systems actionable, especially neural-network visualization methods that identify regions of interest through occlusion or activation back-propagation for debugging training and validating trained model behavior?

evidence.quote: Regarding interpretability, NN visualization [23] shows great promise. In NN visualization, one method intentionally performs occlusion on input data, and specifies the region where the inference result changes drastically as a region of interest; another method back-propagates activation values from the influencer nodes at the later feature extraction process to identify the region of interest. NN visualization may have use in cases of debugging during training, and validation of the training result (understanding the internal behavior of the trained NN). Therefore, one open problem is obtaining concrete use cases to address the interpretability and transparency of safety-critical machine-learning systems, by using NN visualization, interpretation, transparency methods.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a safety-critical system whose decisions depend on a trained neural network classifier f: X -> Y, where X is a space of input signals (e.g., images) and Y a finite set of labels. Two standard neural-network visualization techniques are available:

(i) Occlusion-based saliency: for an input x in X, define a region-of-interest map S_occ(x) by masking subregions of x with a baseline value and recording where f's output probability for the predicted class changes most sharply.

(ii) Activation back-propagation: starting from highly activated nodes in deeper feature-extraction layers of f, back-propagate activation values to the input space to obtain a region-of-interest map S_bp(x).

Formulate and exhibit concrete, well-defined use cases in which the maps S_occ and S_bp can be employed as actionable tools for (a) debugging the network during training and (b) validating the behavior of the trained network, in such a way that the visualizations provide verifiable interpretability and transparency guarantees suitable for safety-critical deployment. Specifically, describe operational procedures, acceptance criteria, and quantitative metrics under which these visualization methods yield decisions about model correctness that can be incorporated into a safety assurance argument.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is engineering-oriented and remains an active open challenge in the safety-critical ML community. There is no canonical solution; ongoing work on saliency-map evaluation and assurance cases (e.g., literature on XAI for safety, ISO/PAS 21448, AMLAS) continues to seek concrete actionable use cases, but no consensus solution exists.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem framed: concrete use cases for NN visualization, interpretation, and transparency methods in safety-critical ML.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem with no provided solution.
